Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`aff8169c-8262-4768-9ad5-2b2422694c1b`](aff8169c-8262-4768-9ad5-2b2422694c1b).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `42e52426064aa26d6a245b96e7a9f3bcdaebafdc` of `main`. The dispatcher refuses to clone (so this PR would not exist) unless both hold at dispatch time: the worker checkout's own revision is a confirmed, current ancestor of local `main` (`worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`), and `main` itself is a confirmed ancestor-or-equal of its own tracking upstream -- carries no commit absent from it (`dispatch.ensure_base_ref_current`; `BaseRefStatus.wrong`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

This attempt resumed from preserved work: the latest of https://github.com/grantbest/homelabv2/pull/1177 was applied as the clone's starting point before the worker's first action (OPS-106). The revision above is the base the baseline was applied onto, not the tree verification ran against -- that tree is base + baseline + this attempt's work.

## Intent

R26.12 (docs/releases/R26.12.json, opens 2026-10-06; design docs/plans/2026-09-23-design-r2612-steerable-and-legible.md, DECIDED by the Operator 2026-09-24; sprint plan docs/plans/2026-09-25-sprints-55-57-the-queue-has-an-order-and-work-in-it.md with P1-P4 decided 2026-09-25). Common rules: dispatch.py and guards.py together are 8,530 lines at main 447d6174 and every merge must stay strictly below 8,556 (the arc budget), net negative at close [RE-BASELINED 2026-10-02 by the outer loop: the pair stood at 8,612 (7,229 + 1,383) at main 856071fe, so the absolute 8,556 no longer binds; the binding size rule is each bead's own net-growth bound in its ACs, measured against its own merge-base, and the arc closes at or below 8,612]; B2 (bead 7f41c574, spec S55-B2) creates apps/factory-dispatcher/queue_order.py and B7 (bead 75b459ca, spec S55-B7) adds rank_pending, RankPolicy, QueuePosition and QueueOrder to it, both PENDING and not merged at this drafting -- if queue_order.py or the names this spec builds on do not exist at your base, the predecessor has not merged: STOP and report unverified, do not re-implement them. Tests use the committed fixtures (tests/fixtures/queue-synthetic-2026-09-23.json, queue-2026-09-23-latched.json, release-inputs-2026-09-23.json, on main since #1026) and doubles only; never a store, a cluster or the live queue (decision record 2026-09-13 D7). The store-double ceiling tests/test_store_double_call_surface.py MAX_HAND_ROLLED_DOUBLES is 35 with zero headroom and counts cross-file subclasses and apps/mcp-hub/tests: extend an existing fake in place, add no new class carrying two or more store-protocol method names. Every spawn passes env= and every new spawn-bearing function gets a CASES entry in tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py. Stage new files with git add before the final verification run. The sprint plan's release order step 4 (:52): '--explain-order, read-only, plus the FACTORY_QUEUE_ORDER=fifo kill switch, outside the budgeted files', landing BEFORE B8 wires rank_pending into pick_task, so that the day B8 merges the operator can read what the order would be and can switch it off without a revert, and so that B8's own pre-merge rails (:53-55: the rank only reorders the selectable set and never drops a bead; a fallback to FIFO on any rank error; the gate-time comparison the outer loop runs) have their mechanism already tested. The design places --explain-order in operator_verbs.py (:77, :82) which does not exist at 447d6174; dispatch.py's CLI gains its flag in B8 within B8's +30 budget, so this bead creates operator_verbs.py with its own entry point (`python operator_verbs.py explain-order`) and touches neither dispatch.py nor guards.py. B7's rank_pending(tasks, *, notes_by_id, release_by_task_id, time_box_by_release_ref, policy, now, claimable_since_by_task_id, impact_by_outcome=None, claimable_since_source='injected', computed_by_revision=None) is the contract this bead reads (release_by_task_id maps task id to guards.ReleaseState, which carries ref and state only, guards.py:665; time_box_by_release_ref carries each release's opened_at and target_at keyed by ref, read from the arch.release beads' content); B7's AC-15 promises every test call goes through one helper so a later argument can be added -- this bead adds none.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: THE KILL SWITCH IS A PURE FUNCTION OF AN EXPLICIT ENVIRON. queue_order.order_mode(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> Literal['rank', 'fifo'] returns 'fifo' when FACTORY_QUEUE_ORDER is exactly 'fifo' (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped), 'rank' when unset or 'rank', and raises ValueError naming the value otherwise (a typo must not silently pick either). It never reads os.environ itself (B7's AC-12 import and IO guard extends to it). Tests cover unset, 'rank', 'fifo', 'FIFO ', and 'off' (refused).
- AC-2: RANK OR FIFO, NEVER NEITHER. queue_order.rank_or_fifo(mode, **rank_pending's keyword inputs) returns a QueueOrder and adds no keyword of its own beyond mode: in 'rank' mode it is rank_pending's result; in 'fifo' mode it is the selectable set in created_at order with every position's explanation reading 'FIFO (FACTORY_QUEUE_ORDER=fifo)' and inputs_unavailable empty; and when rank_pending raises ANY exception in 'rank' mode it returns the FIFO order with the exception's type and message recorded in a new QueueOrder field fallback_reason (None otherwise), never raising. Conservation: a test asserts over both committed fixtures that the SET of task ids in ranked plus held is identical between rank mode and fifo mode, so the rank only reorders and never drops a bead (the plan's first rail). A test injects a rank_pending that raises and asserts the FIFO result with fallback_reason set.
- AC-3: EXPLAIN-ORDER, READ-ONLY. apps/factory-dispatcher/operator_verbs.py exists with `explain-order [--json] [--now ISO]` that builds rank_or_fifo's inputs through an injectable reader (default: the BeadStore GET methods the dispatcher's tick already uses for pending tasks, notes and arch.release beads; time_box_by_release_ref from each arch.release bead's content opened_at and target_at; claimable_since_by_task_id from schedule_status._became_claimable_at over list_events per pending bead, imported by operator_verbs directly -- queue_order imports nothing new, B7 AC-12) and prints the ranked table (position, task id, priority, effective_priority, urgency, release_ref, target_at, class_source, waiting_since, age_days, aged_steps), then the held list with every hold reason, then each position's explanation; --json prints QueueOrder.to_json(). It performs no write: the tests reuse tests/test_schedule_status_waiting_queue.py's existing fake store, which already has list_events, extended in place where a method is missing (no new double: the ceiling is 35 of 35), built from the synthetic fixture, and assert zero non-GET calls and the exact table; a second test asserts the printed order equals rank_pending's over the same inputs. The policy is read from docs/releases/policy/health-policy.json relative to the repo root (B0b) through RankPolicy.from_mapping with policy_revision = the file's git blob sha computed in process; a missing or unreadable policy file prints 'unknown: policy_unreadable' and exits 2, never a default (PRIN-015).
- AC-4: UNWIRED. dispatch.pick_task, the claim-time re-check and every activity are unchanged; a test asserts no production module other than operator_verbs.py imports rank_or_fifo or order_mode. dispatch.py and guards.py are byte-identical to the base (the PR body quotes both `wc -l`).
- AC-5: MUTATION. Each turns a test red: 'off' silently selecting rank; a rank error propagating instead of falling back; fallback_reason left None on a fallback; fifo mode dropping a held bead; explain-order making a write; a default policy used when the file is missing.
- AC-6: REPORT. The PR body states the collected-test count before and after, both line counts, and the exact command an operator runs to read the order and to switch it off (export FACTORY_QUEUE_ORDER=fifo in the dispatcher's env file, then the worker restart the runtime notes require).

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

Mutation: added `reverse=True` to `_fifo_order`'s sort — this test went red (confirmed, then reverted).

2. **FIFO must not share rank's parse failure (AC-2).** Fixed in production: `_fifo_waiting_since` and `_fifo_age_days` in queue_order.py now catch the `ValueError`/`TypeError` that an unparsable/missing `created_at` or a naive `now` previously raised, falling back to epoch UTC / `waiting_since_source="unparsable_created_at"` / `age_days=0` instead of propagating. Both pass; before the fix both raised inside the fallback itself.
